- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 3-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at +3–5% above prior high.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; apply downward bias of 1–2% to forecast tail.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast mid-range.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; adjust forecast to align with sentiment’s “reversal signal” (e.g., sentiment drops below 0.53 → reduce forecast slope).
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment drops sharply within 5 days, adjust forecast 3–5 days ahead to reflect sentiment decay.
